newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - ADtranz unveils new locomotive, sees profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - ADtranz unveils new locomotive, sees profit.

text.p: ADtranz and General Electric Transportation Systems unveiled a new diesel-electric locomotive on Tuesday and said it expected to report a profit for 1996.
Rail technology firm ADtranz is a joint venture between Swiss/Swedish ABB Ltd, German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG and General Electric (GE).
The group spent 12 months developing the new Blue Tiger locomotive, designed to compete in a market estimated at more than $1 billion by the end of the century.
Blue Tiger is considered a light-weight model at 108 tonnes and has a top speed of 200 kilometers per hour.

"This quantum leap in technology gives us an edge that cannot be underestimated," said Kaare Vagner, ADtranz chief executive officer. "It was possible to limit axle loads to under 25 tonnes for all planned configurations of the locomotive while maintaining the structural strength of the unit."
ADtranz was responsible for the locomotive's overall system design, GE developed the engine system.

The companies said Pakistan Railway had placed the first order for the Blue Tiger, ordering 30 six-axle, 3,000 horse power units from Marubeni Corp. to be built by GE and ADtranz and delivered in mid-1998.
Vagner said the group also was in talks with German railway Deutsche Bahn. He said he expected strong demand for the locomotive from developing countries.
He also forecast ADtranz, which was formed late last year, would have sales of around seven billion marks ($4.7 billion) in 1996.
"We will report a black figure in 1996 and a higher profit in 1997," he said.
